_comment: The editorial half of the design pack. build-pack.mjs merges this with the tokens it parses out of night-shift/tokens/*.css to produce pack.json. Everything here is a judgement a parser cannot make: what a colour MEANS, what a component is FOR, and what a builder must not do. Everything derivable from the source stays out of this file so it cannot drift.
name: Night Shift
premise: Most poker products sell a casino: green felt, gold, a room you are lucky to be in. This one is designed for the truth of how the game is played, which is one-handed, in poor light, late. The room is a warm dark you can sit in for an hour, and exactly one saturated cool accent means it is your turn.
north_stars: The table is the product. Everything that is not cards, chips or people is overhead.
Money is information, not spectacle. Figures line up, never jitter, never celebrate at you.
It is play money and it says so. No near-miss theatre, no manufactured urgency.
Legible one-handed, in the dark. Contrast and target size are structural, not audited later.
Motion reports state. A screenshot of the table looks identical to the table at rest.

roles.ns-felt: the deepest ground, the table itself; never pure black
roles.ns-raised: a panel lifted off the ground: a seat, a card of content
roles.ns-raised-2: a control resting on a panel; the quiet button ground
roles.ns-line-soft: a divider inside a panel, quieter than ns-line
roles.ns-muted: labels, meta, anything that must not compete
roles.ns-signal: THE SIGNAL. It means the clock is waiting on you, and nothing else. Never a brand, header or highlight colour.
roles.ns-signal-dim: the signal at rest: a ring or border that is not the lit state
roles.ns-signal-glow: the wash behind a seat on the clock
roles.ns-win: a hand won; a figure that went up
roles.ns-lose: a hand lost; a destructive control
roles.ns-warn: a real warning, never manufactured urgency
roles.ns-cardface: the one bright surface in the room: the face of a playing card
roles.ns-suit-red: hearts, and diamonds in a two-colour deck
roles.ns-suit-black: spades, and clubs in a two-colour deck
roles.ns-card-back: the back of a face-down card
roles.ns-chip-edge: the inset ring that reads as a chip's milled edge

group_notes.type: Two voices: a grotesque for interface, a mono for every figure. Figures are tabular by default so a stack counting down never shifts its row.
group_notes.space: A 4px base. ns-tap is the one non-negotiable: every actionable control is at least 44px effective.
group_notes.radius: Five steps plus full. Cards and chips take the geometry the table needs, not the geometry a card component wants.
group_notes.elevation: The room is dark, so surfaces lift with light rather than shadow. Only a playing card casts a real shadow.
group_notes.table: The table's own measurements. A card is 62x88 and a chip is 38, so a stack of six overlaps into a readable object.
group_notes.motion: Two durations and one curve. Nothing loops, nothing pulses, nothing glows to attract. Under prefers-reduced-motion both durations collapse to 1ms and the state change still happens.

components.name: Button
components.usage: At most ONE variant=act per screen: the thing the clock is waiting on. fold is deliberately the least loud control on a bar, because a product that shouts fold is steering the player. The label always says what happens including the amount: 'Call 4,000', never 'OK'.
components.a11y: min-height is ns-tap. Focus is the system-wide signal outline.

components.name: Badge
components.usage: Only tone=turn may wear the signal colour. A badge always carries the word as well as the colour, which is what makes it the fix for anything otherwise said in colour alone.

components.name: Figure
components.role: a number a player reads under time pressure
components.usage: Every figure in the product goes through this or the ns-figure class. Tabular mono, so a counting stack never shifts the row around it.

components.name: PlayingCard
components.role: the one bright surface in the room
components.usage: Flat, with one real shadow because it is the only object that sits above the table. No flip skeuomorphism. The four-colour deck is a setting, not a default.

components.name: ChipStack
components.usage: Flat overlapping discs, never a bar chart and never a 3D render. The value is printed on every disc as well as coloured, because colour alone is not a label. The whole stack carries the amount as its accessible name.

components.name: Seat
components.usage: When the clock is on this seat it is the only lit thing on the table, and the state is carried three ways at once: a ring, a glow, and the words 'your turn'. Never the ring alone.

components.name: PotDisplay
components.role: the pot; it counts, it never performs
components.usage: The figure counts up over ns-m-move and stops. No coin shower, no celebration that outlasts the information. Under prefers-reduced-motion it sets the final value directly.

components.name: ActionBar
components.role: the three things a player can do
components.usage: Fold, check-or-call, raise. The call button is the single accented control and its label carries the amount.

rules: ns-signal means the clock is waiting on you. It is never a brand colour, a header colour or a highlight. The moment it means two things it means nothing.
Win, loss and warning have their own semantic colours precisely so the signal never has to share duty.
At most one accented action per screen.
Anything said with colour is also said with a word.
Every value in a stylesheet is a var(--ns-*). A raw hex or pixel value the token layer already carries is a bug; if the layer is missing something, add it there.
Every actionable control is at least 44px effective, and focus is always visible in the signal colour.
Figures are tabular mono and never jitter. A screenshot at rest looks identical to the table at rest.
Honour prefers-reduced-motion: durations collapse, the state change still happens.
The room is warm and dark, never pure black; the signal is the only cool thing in it.
refuses: coin-shower wins and celebrations that outlast the information
countdown urgency that is not a real clock
near-miss framing on a lost hand
the signal colour used for anything but the clock waiting on you

voice.tone: Plain and exact. It states what happened and what it costs. It never congratulates the player on losing.
voice.labels: Uppercase mono for labels and counts; sentence case for titles and body.
voice.numbers: Monospace with tabular alignment wherever digits line up. Amounts are grouped: 200,000, never 200000.
voice.money: Play money, stated plainly. Chips, never a currency symbol.
